handoff.purpose: Cache-assisted parallel analysis for pending records, fallback serial, and build_index function setup for documents and types.

symbols.name: _compute
symbols.note: Internal function to analyze pending records in parallel or serial depending on worker count and pending size.

symbols.name: build_index
symbols.note: Main entry point to build the full index, collecting source and document files, applying scope, and preparing data structures.

claims.text: Fill ``out[i]`` for every pending record, in parallel when it pays.
claims.why: The function iterates over pending records and assigns out[i] = analyze_file(...) either in parallel via ProcessPoolExecutor or serial fallback.

claims.text: No usable pool (sandbox, spawn failure, unpicklable payload): the serial path is always correct, just slower.
claims.why: The except block catches any exception from the pool and falls back to serial execution, which is guaranteed to produce the same results.

claims.text: Any None here means a worker silently dropped a file -- recompute inline rather than shipping a short/misaligned list to the clone passes.
claims.why: The for loop after cache.close() checks for None in out and recomputes using analyze_file for those indices.

claims.text: Off unless asked for -- see ``documents_enabled`` above for the measurement that decided that. When off, nothing below this flag executes and the returned dict is byte-identical to the pre-document build.
claims.why: The comment references documents_enabled function and a measurement not present in this chunk; the claim about byte-identical output cannot be verified without seeing the rest of the function.
The claim about wiki edges depending on documents is not verifiable from this chunk alone; it depends on how wiki_on is used later in the function.

claims.text: Resolved here, ONCE, next to ``docs_on`` and for the same reason: the flag decides the shape of the returned dict, so it must be a single boolean that the cache key and the build both read. Resolution and publication are gated; per-file extraction is not (see ``types_enabled``).
claims.why: The comment refers to cache key and types_enabled usage not present in this chunk; the claim about single boolean and gating cannot be verified.

claims.text: Shell files are deliberately still collected and still parsed: they stay in the file-set indexes below, so a real file importing INTO the shell resolves to a true edge instead of silently degrading to 'external'. What they are withheld from is every METRIC -- see the aggregation loop. Doing it this way costs ~2% (the per-file parse) and saves ~96% (clone passes).
claims.why: The claim about shell files being included in indexes but excluded from metrics, and the performance percentages, cannot be verified from this chunk alone; they depend on code not present here.

claims.text: A vendored/spec-copy doc tree is shell for exactly the reasons a vendored source tree is; a new node kind does not get to walk around the boundary.
claims.why: The claim about doc_ignored being shell for the same reasons as source ignored cannot be verified without seeing the scope.is_shell implementation.

claims.text: A center root is also a PACKAGE root, so files under it are named relative to it; everything else keeps repo-root naming. See ``_PyNaming`` for why this is not one global table.
claims.why: The claim about naming conventions and _PyNaming class cannot be verified without seeing the _PyNaming definition and usage.

claims.text: File-set indexes for best-effort non-Python import resolution (Move 2).
claims.why: The claim about Move 2 and best-effort resolution cannot be verified without seeing the rest of the function where these indexes are used.

observations.what: The _compute function uses _worker_count and _parallel_min which are not defined in this chunk; they must be defined elsewhere in the module.
The build_index function references _collect_docs, documents_enabled, wiki_enabled, types_enabled, project_scope, _PyNaming which are not defined in this chunk; they must be defined or imported.
The final fallback loop (lines 478-480) recomputes analyze_file for any None in out after cache.close(), which could overwrite results if analyze_file returned None from the parallel path.
The comment about 'docs_on' being off unless asked for and returning byte-identical dict cannot be verified from this chunk alone.
